Relationship: Stoltzenberg → supplied chemical weapons capability to → Spain against the Rif
Evidence: Approach of 20 Aug 1921 for mustard gas in breach of Versailles; first delivery 1923; later Spanish nationality and involvement in building La Marañosa. Documented in Kunz & Müller (1990) and Balfour (2002).

Relationship: Ba Ahmed → regent for → Moulay Abdelaziz
Evidence: Effective ruler of Morocco for six years; the sultan was systematically excluded from government until Ba Ahmed's death in 1900.

Relationship: Hassan I → appointed → Ma al-'Aynayn as khalifa of the Sahara
Evidence: A dahir appointing him representative over Saharan territories. The date determines whether the act preceded or responded to Spanish occupation at Dakhla — which is the crux of the modern territorial argument.

Relationship: Lyautey → obtained the abdication of → Moulay Abdelhafid
Evidence: Abdication secured against a large pension; Moulay Youssef installed in his place, chosen for having no independent base.

Relationship: Poeymirau → received the submission of → the sons of Mouha ou Hammou
Evidence: Hassan and Amharoq submitted, followed by c. 3,000 tents. The claim that they did so on their father's advice is a single-source assertion. The terms of the submission have not been located.

Relationship: Franco → launched the 1936 coup from → Morocco
Evidence: Career made in the Rif war; Legion commander at the Alhucemas landing 1925; airlifted the Army of Africa, Legion and Moroccan Regulares, to the peninsula. Self-referential entry recording the fact that the Spanish Civil War began in Morocco.

Relationship: Ba Ahmed → concealed the death of → Hassan I
Evidence: Chamberlain and grand vizier; concealed the sultan's death on 9 June 1894 while the column was in unsecured country, continuing to issue orders in his name, then proclaimed Abdelaziz. Duration of the concealment is not established.

Relationship: Lyautey → patron of → Thami El Glaoui
Evidence: The central client relationship of the politique des grands caïds: France armed, enriched and protected him against rivals, producing authority greater than any pre-Protectorate qaid could have held.

Relationship: Moulay Abdelhafid → captured and executed → Bou Hamara
Evidence: Fact and year established; brought to Fez in a cage. The manner of execution is disputed — the widely repeated 'fed to his lions' account is poorly sourced, and shooting and public display also appear.

Relationship: Hassan I → appointed → Mouha ou Hammou Zayani
Evidence: Reference literature records the investiture as qaid of the Zaian, brokered by the Sherqawa marabout Sidi Ben Dawd, with a black cloak, sharifian infantry and artillery. Three different years appear in works of comparable authority.

Relationship: Laverdure → fought → Mouha ou Hammou Zayani at El Herri
Evidence: Column of 43 officers and 1,187 men; 623 killed including Laverdure. Marched without orders. Two of Hammou's wives captured, later exchanged for the bodies of Laverdure and six officers.

Relationship: Oufkir → named as responsible for the abduction of → Mehdi Ben Barka
Evidence: A 1967 French trial convicted two officers of kidnapping and the judge identified Oufkir as principally responsible. The witness Georges Figon, who testified that Oufkir killed Ben Barka, was later found dead. French files remain classified.

Relationship: Moulay Abdelhafid → deposed → Moulay Abdelaziz
Evidence: Proclaimed Marrakech Aug 1907; conditional bay'a of the Fez ulama Jan 1908; Abdelaziz defeated at the Battle of Marrakech 19 Aug 1908, largely by defection, and abdicated two days later.

Relationship: Thami El Glaoui → demanded the deposition of → Mohammed V
Evidence: Public declaration of loyalty to the Protectorate and demand for the sultan's removal, 19 May 1953. Reversed 25 Oct 1955; knelt in submission 8 Nov 1955 and was pardoned. Whether the initiative was his or the Residency's is unsettled.

Relationship: Silvestre → fought → Abd el-Krim at Annual
Evidence: Expediente Picasso findings on over-extension and command failure. Spanish dead given variously as 7,875 to 13,363 depending on definition. Silvestre's manner of death not established.

Relationship: Berenguer → authorised chemical munitions against → the Rif
Evidence: Telegram to War Minister Marichalar, 12 Aug 1921: he would employ such munitions 'con verdadera fruición'. Quoted by Sebastian Balfour from Spanish archives. Not verified at document level by this project. Written three days after Monte Arruit.

Relationship: Guillaume → deposed and exiled → Mohammed V
Evidence: Deposition and exile to Corsica, then Antsirabe in Madagascar, executed under his residency. Three versions of who decided — Paris, Guillaume, or El Glaoui and the notables — remain in circulation and are settleable from the Residency-Paris correspondence.

Relationship: Regnault → negotiated the Treaty of Fez with → Moulay Abdelhafid
Evidence: A negotiation session reported at around six hours on 29 March, with French troops in and around Fez; signed 30 March. Regnault's own reporting to the Quai d'Orsay would establish what pressure was applied and has not been read.

Relationship: Raisuni → abducted → Harry Maclean
Evidence: Ransomed for £20,000 paid by the British government, after Raisuni's removal from the pashalik of Tangier. Note: the date 1907 circulates and appears to be wrong.

Relationship: Si Madani El Glaoui → engineered the accession of → Moulay Abdelhafid
Evidence: Prominent among the southern notables who invited Abdelhafid, then khalifa at Marrakech, to take the throne. Became his grand vizier. His brother Thami was made pasha of Marrakech.

Relationship: Pétain → superseded → Lyautey
Evidence: Sent with overriding authority after Abd el-Krim's April 1925 offensive on the Ouergha; Lyautey resigned. Read structurally, the tache d'huile method had reached its limit against a rival state with an army.

Relationship: Mohammed ben Arafa → installed in place of → Mohammed V
Evidence: Proclaimed by an assembly of notables. Never accepted; two assassination attempts. The bay'a assembled for him, with its signatories and refusals, is a documentable map of elite alignment in 1953.
